title: Null-forgiving operator and ArgumentNullException
hook: The postfix ! does nothing at run time. ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull does. Interviews listen for which one you reach for at an SQS or auth boundary.

sections.heading: Operators that keep you honest
sections.prose: ?. and ?[] skip the member or indexer when the receiver is null. ?? and ??= supply a fallback. is not null / is { } is the preferred test; == null still works but loses pattern narrowing in some generic cases. These operators change control flow. The postfix null-forgiving operator x! does not: Microsoft’s language reference is explicit that x! evaluates as x and only suppresses warnings. Use it when you are writing a unit test that must pass null into a non-nullable parameter, or when you have a proof the analyzer cannot see and you cannot add an attribute. Do not use it on RedisValue.ToString() because ‘the key usually exists.’

snippets.label: Guard an SQS record, do not bang it
snippets.explanation: ThrowIfNull is a runtime guard and a null-state update. Optional attributes stay string?. No ! required.

sections.heading: ThrowIfNull versus handwritten if
sections.prose: ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(argument) uses CallerArgumentExpression so the parameter name is captured without nameof. After the call, analysis treats the argument as not-null — the BCL annotates it with [NotNull]. ThrowIfNullOrWhiteSpace covers tokens and header values. A handwritten if (x is null) throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(x)) is still correct on older TFMs; on .NET 10 prefer the helpers. Guards belong at the public edge of a worker: deserialized SQS body, JWT subject, config connection string. Internal helpers can assume non-null once the edge has thrown.

sections.heading: When ! is legitimate
sections.prose: Tests that assert a constructor throws on null need Person(null!). DI or source generators sometimes produce a non-null value the analyzer cannot follow. If you control the helper, prefer [NotNullWhen(true)] on IsPresent so callers never write !. A codebase where every Redis lookup ends with cache.Get(key)! is a map of places you will page at 2 a.m.

interviewTakeaways: x! is warning suppression with identity semantics at run time.
ThrowIfNull is a real throw plus a [NotNull] post-condition the compiler understands.
?. ?? is not null are the everyday operators; ! is the exception.
commonPitfalls: Using ! to satisfy CS8602 instead of fixing the annotation or adding a check.
Catching NullReferenceException instead of throwing ArgumentNullException at the boundary.
Forgetting that message.Body can be empty even when the Message object is non-null.

jsTsCorrelations.note: TS value! is the same idea: compile-time only. JS still throws if you read .length of null.
?. and ?? exist in JS and C# with similar short-circuit rules. C# also has ThrowIfNull as a standard library guard.
